label: mid-prefix tokens (v/i/t/x/3/1/n/h) after an early f/r/p, sequences starting 0 or c
explanation: Sparse feature (0.05% of steps) that fires almost only in the original-input phase (99% of mass), at steps 3-6 (peak t=4), never at t=0-1 and almost never during copy. It favors first-occurrence inputs from {v,i,t,x,3,1,n,h}, when an f (most strongly two steps back, prev2 lift 15.7x), r or p appeared earlier, and when the sequence starts with 0 or c (first_tok 0 lift 10x). Top examples look like 0/c f f w [i]. Each of these factors alone has precision under 2%. Their conjunction reaches only F1 about 0.21 (precision 0.16, recall 0.31) on dev, so the feature seems to encode a specific hash-like combination of the prefix contents that no simple predicate captures. Magnitude is higher when f sits directly 2 steps before the active token and the sequence starts with 0/c, judging from the top examples. It does not fire on delimiter or copy steps.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=0 (+6.08), orig0=c (+4.57), orig2=f (+3.99), prev_tok=p (+3.60), orig0=i (+3.53), orig1=f (+3.51). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-4.38), t=8 (-4.24), prev_tok=0 (-3.47), prev2_tok=0 (-3.34).
